Established legally binding emissions reduction targets framed around existential climate threat; five-year carbon budgets constrained future democratic choices, reflecting emergency legislation.
Established a permanent Special Resolution Regime that granted the state authority to transfer bank ownership without court authorisation; property rights overridable by ministerial order.

Act: Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011
Securitisation rationale: Replaced control orders with terrorism prevention methods that imposed overnight residence requirements and travel restrictions without criminal conviction.
Introduced the hostile environment regime imposing right-to-rent checks on landlords, NHS surcharges on migrants and restricted appeal rights for immigration decisions.

Act: Data Retention and Investigatory Powers Act 2014
Securitisation rationale: Fast-tracked through Parliament in four days to reinstate bulk data retention after the European Court of Justice invalidated the underlying Directive; extended extraterritorial interception warrant powers.
Introduced temporary exclusion orders for British nationals abroad and imposed a Prevent duty on educational and public institutions; also enhanced passport seizure powers.

Extended the hostile environment regime by criminalising illegal working, creating a new driving offence for those in breach of immigration conditions and expanding immigration officer seizure powers.
Legalised bulk communication interception, equipment interference and 12-month retention of internet connection records.
Extended terrorism offences extraterritorially and made viewing terrorist content online illegal; also introduced hostile state activity powers.

Act: Covert Human Intelligence Sources (Criminal Conduct) Act 2021
Securitisation rationale: Granted statutory authorisation for undercover agents to commit criminal acts without being prosecuted and without prior judicial oversight.
Fast-tracked in two weeks following Russia's invasion of Ukraine to accelerate sanctions implementation; established a Register of Overseas Entities and strengthened Unexplained Wealth Orders.

Act: Police Crime Sentencing and Courts Act 2022
Securitisation rationale: Granted police powers to impose conditions on one-person protests; created offences for causing serious annoyance; extended stop-and-search powers.
Introduced a two-tier asylum system based on mode of arrival, criminalised irregular entry and enabled offshore processing of claims.
Introduced Serious Disruption Prevention Orders, created offences including locking-on and tunnelling and enabled stop-and-search without suspicion at protests.

Repealed the Official Secrets Acts 1911, 1920 and 1939; introduced new offences of foreign interference and assisting a foreign intelligence service, a Foreign Influence Registration Scheme and an expanded prohibited places regime.
Imposed a duty to remove all irregular arrivals, barred asylum claims from those entering via safe third countries and permitted indefinite detention.

Explicitly framed around energy independence as a national security response to Russian gas dependency and introduced compulsory acquisition powers for energy infrastructure outside normal procurement.
Imposed a duty of care on online platforms; granted Ofcom powers to require removal of encryption; mandated age verification; enabled website blocking.
Required technology firms to notify government before changing products, relaxed oversight thresholds for surveillance warrants and also broadened bulk dataset access.

Act: Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act 2024
Securitisation rationale: Mandated treating Rwanda as a safe country by statute, overriding a Supreme Court judgment and disapplying Human Rights Act provisions on refoulement.
